method: Built-in image_gen; sequential reference edits for closely matched composition

connected.prompt: Use case: precise-object-edit and lighting-weather. Create one faithful landscape concept refinement of the attached Carved Alabaster website scene. The reference image is the exact camera, geometry arrangement, portal silhouettes, spiral turns and composition. Keep the same spiral ribbon, portal locations, sizes and orientations, and small central bronze tetrahedron. This is the CONNECTED version. Each portal's lower porcelain frame flows into an extremely small, elegant fitted ceramic joint sitting directly on the ribbon, no gap, no pedestal, no broad support plinth. There is a precise soft contact shadow at the junction and a delicate believable directional cast shadow across the opaque porcelain ribbon. Make the ribbon warm milk-ivory porcelain with a satin tactile finish and very subtle mineral variation, clean rounded bevels and dimensional shaded underside; it must not look like yellow plastic, gold metal or heavily veined marble. Preserve the colored translucent mirror/glass interiors (honey, sage, lavender, blush) and thin champagne inner rim, but no glowing halos. Change the cloud environment to soft PEARL WHITE cumulus with cool pale blue-grey/lavender shadows and a powder-blue upper sky, very pale pearl horizon, only a restrained warm light source on the left. Remove the strong yellow/golden color wash from clouds and sky so their cooler white contrasts with the warm milk-ivory stair. Maintain natural atmospheric cloud detail and plentiful quiet sky. Use coherent soft directional daylight, subtle material depth, no bloom, no lens flare, no text, no labels, no interface, no people or new objects. This is a premium architectural real-time website target, not overprocessed fantasy. Keep framing and aspect ratio identical to the source. Ensure visually clear actual physical contact at the prominent near leaf portal and upper-left tall portal. Do not change camera or move doors.

floating.prompt: Use case: precise-object-edit. This is the FLOATING counterpart to the attached connected porcelain spiral concept. Make only one substantive change: lift every framed mirror/glass portal vertically off the spiral ribbon by about 10–12 percent of its own height, keeping its x/z location, orientation, silhouette, scale and finish. Show an unmistakable, clean AIR GAP between the bottom of every portal and the ribbon underneath. This matters especially at the large foreground sage leaf portal and the tall honey portal at upper left. Remove their ceramic feet/fillets entirely; nothing supports or touches the suspended portals, no pedestal, no wires. Add physically coherent softly edged CAST SHADOWS from the hovering portal silhouettes on the milk-ivory porcelain ribbon below, offset slightly toward the lower-right by the existing upper-left light. The shadow should describe hovering height and make the floating mirrors feel intentional and magical. Keep shadows local and restrained but plainly visible against the porcelain; opaque frame casts a darker shadow and tinted pane a much lighter soft colored component. Do not paint a dark halo around portals. Preserve the EXACT reference camera, spiral shape, turns and ribbon thickness, the central bronze tetrahedron, the pearl-white clouds, powder-blue sky, cool blue-grey cloud shadows, sunlight direction, material palette, and framing. Do not recolor the scene. Do not add extra portals, text, labels, interface, beams, glow or particles. Preserve the premium satin porcelain and fine champagne trim. This is the same composition and lighting as the connected image, with a deliberate visible levitation gap and its cast shadows. Landscape image same aspect ratio.

note: Concept images only. Colors, reflected detail and cast shadows are illustrative, not measured real-time output.
